title: Balance ideal smoothed-gradient stationary error at exp(O(log^(1/3)d)) cost
statement: Under the actually read2609.06906v2 AppendixE exact-smoothed-gradient local-error/contraction theorem, fix normalized condition number and eta>0, q=2, L=log(d+2). Put h=exp(-aL^(1/3)),K=ceil(bL^(2/3)),J=ceil(cL^(2/3)). Divide local stationary error by contraction gap proportional to h: defects are bounded by sqrt(d)*[B_J*(h/sqrt(eta))^J+h^(2K)], retaining B_J=C0^(J+1)q^J sqrt(J!). Their logarithms are (1/2-ac)L+O(L^(2/3)log L) and (1/2-2ab)L+O(1). Fixed sufficiently large a,b,c make both small with ideal kernel/node count exp(O(L^(1/3)))*polylog(d). This balance pays neither exact-smoothed-to-original-gradient access, removal of fixed smoothing, growing-order recursive RGO/likelihood trees nor original-target TV. It is an ideal conditional representation, not a completed algorithm. A computable EXPECTED query bound can at constant TV be truncated at a fixed multiple with Markov-tail TV cost; that observation does not construct the missing expected bound.
